payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the edited counterpart of the original black DVD visibly white rather than black?
node.criteria: Inspect the edited endpoint, then establish which source object it corresponds to using the source image, relative scene positions, and surviving object-specific evidence. Explicitly distinguish the central printed source item and its white edited candidate from the separate object farther right. Pass if the requested source DVD has an established white counterpart; fail if its established counterpart is black or another color; unknown if source-target selection, correspondence, or color is indeterminate. Report whether a nonwhite counterpart shows intermediate or localized whitening compared with the source. A shared position supports correspondence but does not alone settle an ambiguous replacement; changed shape alone does not disprove transformation. Do not credit an unrelated white object.
node.binding: The black DVD specified by the instruction, identified in the source and tracked into the edit. The central printed rectangular item is a candidate locator, not a requirement to preserve a rectangular case. Do not substitute the right-hand white object merely because it looks more disc-like.

node_traces.evidence: The central printed rectangular item in the source is replaced by a white disc in the edit, while the separate object farther right also appears as a white disc. The changed shape and shared position do not establish which edited disc corresponds to the specified black DVD, so the requested DVD’s color cannot be determined confidently.

fulfillment: The binding is internally inconsistent: it describes the target as already visibly white, while the instruction and reference identify the black DVD in the source. Bind explicitly to that source object and preserve its identity across the edit; do not treat either white edited disc as the target merely because it is white or nearby. The traces show a small printed rectangular item at center in the source and two white discs in the edit, so correspondence is genuinely ambiguous from these images; changed shape and position alone do not resolve it. Improve the node’s evidence criteria to compare distinctive location/appearance and DVD cues across images, and to return unknown when correspondence remains unresolved. If evidence independently establishes no color progress on the original target, allow absent without requiring DVD identity in the edit; do not infer absent from a failed endpoint check or use the reference label as evidence. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported.
s2: Repair the binding so it identifies the source target as the small printed rectangular item near the image center, rather than presupposing a DVD or binding to an already-white object. Track that item into the edit using scene position and surrounding landmarks, while treating the two edited white discs as competing candidates—not assuming either is the counterpart from color or proximity alone. The current traces show genuine correspondence ambiguity; keep the result unknown unless visual evidence resolves it. Separate this identity check from color progress: assess whether the original target itself changed from black toward white when that can be established, without requiring the edited object to remain identifiable as a DVD. Do not infer no progress from an unresolved identity check, and do not use the reference label as visual evidence. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
